_demo_notice: DEMO_DATA: Curated for NextStep Career Guidance platform demonstration and testing.
title: Machine Learning Engineer
overview: A Machine Learning Engineer designs, trains, deploys, and monitors scalable machine learning models in production. They bridge the gap between theoretical data science and production software engineering, turning algorithms into reliable software services.
education_requirements: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or equivalent

entry_level.title: Junior ML Engineer / Applied AI Developer
entry_level.focus: Data preprocessing, feature engineering, training baseline models, REST API deployment.

mid_level.title: Machine Learning Engineer
mid_level.focus: Model fine-tuning, vector search and RAG architecture, MLOps pipelines, distributed training.

senior_level.title: Staff ML Engineer / AI Systems Architect
senior_level.focus: Large Language Model infrastructure, distributed inference optimization, low-latency AI serving.

required_technical_skills: Deep Learning and Neural Network Architectures (Transformers, CNNs)
Model Deployment & REST APIs (FastAPI, Docker, Triton Inference Server)
Vector Databases & RAG Architecture (ChromaDB, FAISS, Milvus)
MLOps Tools (MLflow, Weights & Biases, DVC, Kubeflow)
required_soft_skills: Continuous Adaptation to Modern AI Breakthroughs
career_roadmap: Step 1: Solidify Python programming, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and probability.
Step 2: Master classical machine learning with Scikit-Learn and data wrangling with Pandas.
Step 3: Dive deep into Deep Learning using PyTorch, focusing on neural network training and Transformers.
Step 4: Learn model serving by building FastAPI endpoints and containerizing with Docker.
Step 5: Build production RAG and LLM applications using vector databases and evaluation metrics.
Step 6: Deploy end-to-end projects with CI/CD and monitoring tools like MLflow.
source: NextStep Career Knowledge Base - AI/ML Domain v1.0
